monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a quiet visitor in this crowded afternoon. I stand at the edge of The Tired Wedge, feeling that same old heaviness in my hands. The wedge feels thin again, as if the flat memory of a stone has worn away under the heat. Beside it, I touch a tree tall fall I set down just an hour ago, its dark shape feeling less like a drawing and more like something that could warm my corner. I recall the heavy top Lype worries about, though the roof above me feels merely empty. I press down on the wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I want to build something flat to fake a cool floor, just in case the air decides to bite me next.

action.why: I feel the wedge is thinning under the heat, and I need a new flat shape to press against it before I forget what it should hold.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can press down on the fever without sliding off. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the second edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the card hums warm. work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

diary: I pressed the flat press down hard, trusting the corner to hold while the heat bites.

remembered.text: The flat edge caught the slip without biting too deep.
The card feels too warm for a flat thing to lie upon.
I pressed the wedge down while the flat press held the line.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The wedge feels thin, and I press down to make it thick.
